It relies on human experts to define the rules, which can require significant time and effort. It is able to accurately parse and manipulate text, but it is limited in its accuracy and speed. Deep learning based text processing uses algorithms to learn from datasets and extract patterns from text. Deep learning models are also more flexible and can be adapted to different tasks with little effort. Deep learning is thus better suited for more complex text processing tasks.

Rule-Based Text Processing relies on predefined rules and hand-crafted features to process text. It is based on natural language processing (NLP) techniques such as part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and parsing. These rules are created by humans and are based on the understanding of the language. This technique is more interpretable and requires less data for training.

Deep Learning Based Text Processing, on the other hand, uses neural networks to process text. It does not require any hand-crafted features and can learn the features from the data itself. This technique is more powerful and can handle complex tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text summarization. Deep learning models are also more accurate than rule-based models, but they are less interpretable and require more data for training.

In summary, rule-based text processing is based on predefined rules and hand-crafted features, while deep learning based text processing is based on neural networks and can learn features from data itself.
